notes.claim: In a pure inductor the voltage leads the current, that is, the current lags behind the voltage.
Inductive reactance is X_L = 2πfL, in ohms, and is directly proportional to the frequency of the alternating current.
Inductors oppose changes in current through them by dropping a voltage directly proportional to the rate of change of current, where resistors drop one proportional to the current.
A 10 mH inductor has a reactance of 3.7699 ohms at 60 Hz, 7.5398 ohms at 120 Hz and 157.0796 ohms at 2500 Hz.
High power electric motors are inductive loads (Matrix electrical installation Level 3 teacher guide, SECONDARY).
A City & Guilds 2366 sample question asks for the inductive reactance of a 20 mH inductor on a 50 Hz supply (6.28 ohms, computed from X_L = 2πfL).

sources.quote: What this means is that reactance in ohms for any inductor is directly proportional to the frequency of the alternating current.

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 3
sources.quote: Whereas resistors simply oppose the flow of electrons through them (by dropping a voltage directly proportional to the current), inductors oppose changes in current through them, by dropping a voltage directly proportional to the rate of change of current.
